items.claim: A password-reset request that carries both a reset token and a separate username parameter is the test case for token/account binding: changing the username field lets the tester set a new password for an account the token was never issued to.
items.body:
A password-reset request that carries both a reset token and a separate username parameter is the test case for token/account binding: changing the username field lets the tester set a new password for an account the token was never issued to.

HackTricks reference: 376f3c60 (notion:376f3c60-4cee-43b6-a488-dac183d8cfc9)
items.disproof: The reset request rejects a username that does not own the token, or the new password only authenticates the token's original owner.

items.claim: Web cache poisoning hunting starts from request parameters the cache key omits, and the values that get reflected into the underlying application — a reflected XSS or host header injection point — are what make such an unkeyed parameter dangerous.
items.body:
Web cache poisoning hunting starts from request parameters the cache key omits, and the values that get reflected into the underlying application — a reflected XSS or host header injection point — are what make such an unkeyed parameter dangerous.

HackTricks reference: 29e098c3 (notion:29e098c3-95c5-80e9-8d84-e2369fc415b9)
items.disproof: Every parameter that influences the response turns out to be part of the cache key, so no unkeyed input can be used to poison a cached entry.
